steps.action: Posed the question of how absorbing boundary conditions affect effectiveness and computational cost in the full FWI problem, beyond the forward problem where they are usually assessed.
steps.quote: the overall impact of ABCs on the full-waveform inversion problem, from the perspective of computational cost-effectiveness and efficiency, is still widely debated

steps.action: Set up the published rival ABCs (Sochacki damping, Grote-Sim PML, Pasalic-McGarry CPML, Liu-Sen HABC-A1) as the alternatives to be compared.
steps.quote: The analyses are carried out for two types of ABCs, namely, sponge layers

steps.action: Proposed a hybrid ABC that nests order-2 Higdon conditions (angles 0 and pi/4) over successive one-grid-line domain extensions combined by nonlinear convex weights.
steps.quote: Furthermore, we propose a HABC approach, based on the Higdon method

steps.action: Derived the adjoint wave equations and adjoint boundary conditions for each ABC from the augmented Lagrangian functional (Sect. 4, Appendix A).
steps.quote: we have formally derived adjoint boundary conditions that correspond to each of the ABCs

steps.action: Implemented all ABCs in Devito using high-level symbolic code, solving the extra ABC equations only on subdomains in the extension region.
steps.quote: The possibility of creating specific subdomains allows us to save time and memory for the computations.

steps.action: Designed the test: reflection-free reference solutions on a very large domain, a relative L2 error (Eq. 33) on the physical domain, four heterogeneous velocity models, and extension width p from 1 to 20 percent.
steps.quote: The goal of this particular and very large extended region is solely to define adequate reference solutions with no inbound reflected waves.

steps.action: Compared forward-solution errors of the five ABCs against the reference as a function of Ricker peak frequency for the four velocity models.
steps.quote: It is also clear in Fig. that the HABC-Higdon incurs smaller errors.

steps.action: Varied the domain-extension width p at several peak frequencies for the Marmousi and SEG/EAGE models to check whether the ranking held.
steps.quote: In order to ascertain whether similar behaviour would be seen for different sizes of domain extension

steps.action: Compared adjoint-solution errors of each ABC against a reflection-free adjoint reference, with forcing from true minus guess velocity models, as a function of peak frequency.
steps.quote: In several cases, HABC-Higdon errors are either close to or smaller than the PML errors.

steps.action: Varied extension width p for the adjoint problem at several peak frequencies.
steps.quote: In all cases, the error diminishes as p increases.

steps.action: Kept the sub-claim that the adjoint problem has its own spurious boundary reflections plus those carried over from the forward solution through the forcing term.
steps.quote: the adjoint problem experiences its own spurious boundary reflections

steps.action: Measured wall-clock time and memory growth of each ABC relative to a no-ABC Dirichlet baseline on Marmousi, and plotted error against cost.
steps.quote: Also, for p > 1 , HABC-Higdon demands less wall clock time and memory usage than that of PML and CPML

steps.action: Selected damping, PML and HABC-Higdon for full FWI tests on Marmousi with L-BFGS-B, with the extension width set as max(c)/f.
steps.quote: this section proposes to compare numerical results and the computational cost in FWI using damping, PML, and HABC-Higdon

steps.action: Compared misfit, velocity-model error and cost of FWI runs at f0 = 7 Hz across the ABCs.
steps.quote: Therefore, it is proper to conclude that HABC-Higdon has shown better overall performance compared to PML.

end.claim: A hybrid ABC with nested Higdon conditions is as effective as or more effective than PML and the other schemes at suppressing boundary reflections in forward, adjoint and FWI problems, at lower computational cost.

decisive_move.sentence: The reflection-free reference solutions computed on a very large domain, with the relative error of Eq. (33), are what make ABC effectiveness measurable and the ranking possible.

gates.evidence: The objective of proposing a cheaper and effective ABC (§1 ¶6) shaped the choice of experiments, but no hypothesis directed data acquisition beyond the benchmark design. The ranking could have failed against the reference errors and cost baselines, and it partly did: PML had lower velocity error at the 5 and 8 Hz cuts (§7 ¶7). No thresholds or analyses were fixed in advance. HABC weights and alpha follow Liu and Sen (2018), and the nonlinear weights were chosen after observing better results (§3.5 ¶8).

limits:
Composition none_fits: the paper is a numerical benchmark of named rival methods plus a proposed new method, ranked by measured error and cost against a reference. There is no crucial test with predicted outcomes (not strong_inference), and the rivals precede the capability (not capability_first). No review file or discussion was supplied; the review statement names two anonymous referees, so no review sequence is coded.

Sub-claims and their statuses:
- The adjoint problem experiences its own spurious reflections: regularity_in_range, simulation evidence on four models.
- CPML is less effective in the adjoint problem: regularity_in_range, in the tested range.
- The ABC ranking extends to 3D, real seismograms, and elastic or other wave physics: none. These are argued from symmetry and cited literature, not tested here (§8 ¶5-7).

Results come from single deterministic runs with no uncertainty or repeated timing statistics reported (inference). Timings come from one machine. In the FWI tests the true data are synthetic, and the true data and the inversion share the same solver family (inverse-crime risk, inference). The FWI comparison covers only Marmousi. The multiscale case is mixed (PML better at 5 and 8 Hz), yet the headline claim stays unqualified in the abstract. HABC parameters were taken from Liu and Sen (2018) and the weight choice was made after observing results; the process of tuning is not documented (inference). The adjoint test uses an initial-guess forcing rather than FWI iterates.
